_meta.status: Curated reference snapshots used by the chip shortcuts in AlertPanel. Numbers + EMS IDs are placeholders awaiting NIMH verification by Elitsa. See specs/06-history-replay/01-design.md.
_meta.why_baked: Many of these events are basin-driven (Danube snowmelt, Carpathian rain) and won't classify correctly from local point precipitation alone — hence we ship pre-baked snapshots for the demo narrative while the calendar handles meteorology-driven dates with real ERA5 data.
_meta.schema: Each event mirrors the extractor return-dict (10-key contract) so AlertPanel renders identically to a live assessment.

pleven.name: Skat / Mizia basin floods
pleven.summary: Convective storms dropped >120mm in 24h on already-saturated soils; Skat tributary breached, Mizia inundated.

snapshot.source: Curated from EMSR094 + ERA5 reanalysis (TODO: NIMH-verify)

pleven.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 1 August 2014.** Northern Bulgaria received over **120 mm of rainfall in 24 hours** following a wet July that had already saturated soils across Pleven Oblast.

- **Soil moisture:** 92% — well above the 85% FLOOD_WARNING threshold
- **7-day precipitation:** 165 mm — convective system stationary over the upper basin
- **River level:** Skat tributary peaked at 6.8 m, breaching the Mizia levees
- **Flood extent:** 18.5 km² inundated (Sentinel-1 GRD, post-event)

Three of three FLOOD_WARNING thresholds breached. Casualties recorded in Mizia town.

pleven.name: Danube basin spring flood (100-year level)
pleven.summary: Snowmelt + sustained rainfall pushed the Danube to its highest level in over a century at Nikopol.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH river gauge archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

pleven.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 15 April 2006.** A combination of late-Carpathian snowmelt and persistent rainfall over the upper Danube catchment drove water levels at Nikopol to **9.2 m**, the highest reading in over a century.

- **Danube level:** 9.2 m at Nikopol gauge — exceeded the 100-year return period
- **Soil moisture:** 95% saturation, no infiltration capacity left
- **30-day precipitation:** 240 mm across the Danube basin
- **Inundation:** 32 km² in the Nikopol floodplain

FLOOD_WARNING with maximum confidence — Pleven Oblast's Danube border was the most exposed segment of the Bulgarian coastline.

pleven.name: Spring snowmelt floods (Vit & Osam basins)
pleven.summary: Late snowmelt across the Stara Planina compounded by sustained May rainfall raised tributaries above seasonal norms.
pleven.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 17 May 2010.** The 2010 spring saw above-average snowpack in the Stara Planina ridge feeding the **Vit and Osam tributaries** in Pleven Oblast.

- **Soil moisture:** 84% — at the FLOOD_WATCH threshold
- **River level:** Vit at 5.4 m (1.1 m above seasonal baseline)
- **30-day precipitation:** 175 mm — second-wettest May on local record
- **Flood extent:** 4.2 km² localised inundation in low-lying farmland

Two of three FLOOD_WATCH thresholds breached. No casualties reported.

pleven.name: Bulgarian heatwave & agricultural drought
pleven.summary: Record temperatures (>44°C) and a near-zero July rainfall total devastated cereal yields across northern Bulgaria.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH temperature archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

pleven.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 24 July 2007.** Pleven recorded one of the highest temperatures in Bulgarian history during a multi-week heatwave that desiccated topsoil across the Danubian Plain.

- **Temperature:** 44°C peak — exceeded the DROUGHT_WARNING heat threshold
- **30-day precipitation:** 8 mm — effectively zero infiltration
- **Soil moisture:** 14% — wilting point reached for shallow-rooted crops
- **NDVI:** 0.22 — vegetation collapse across non-irrigated fields
- **SPI-3 (drought index):** 2.8 — severe meteorological drought

Compound drought-heat event. Cereal harvest losses estimated >40% regionally.

pleven.name: August 2005 northern Bulgaria floods
pleven.summary: One of three major flood waves in the wettest summer on Bulgarian record; Vit and Osam basins overflowed.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH gauge archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

pleven.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 7 August 2005.** The 2005 summer was the wettest on Bulgarian record, with three distinct flood waves across the Danubian Plain.

- **7-day precipitation:** 110 mm — third successive 100mm+ week
- **Soil moisture:** 86% — beyond field capacity
- **River level:** Osam at 5.8 m (1.5 m above seasonal mean)
- **Flood extent:** 6.1 km² localised, primarily agricultural

FLOOD_WATCH escalation likely had a fourth wave materialised — close call between thresholds.

burgas.name: August 2014 Burgas coastal flash floods
burgas.summary: Intense convective storms dropped >100 mm in 6 h over Burgas city; streets and the Mandra-Poda wetland buffer overflowed.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH gauge archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

burgas.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 8 August 2014.** A quasi-stationary convective system over the Black Sea coast delivered **over 100 mm in 6 hours** on top of already-saturated soils, overwhelming Burgas city drainage and the Mandra-Poda coastal buffer.

- **7-day precipitation:** 148 mm — convective system stalled over the coastal plain
- **Soil moisture:** 91% — field capacity exceeded across the lowland
- **River level:** Aytoska river at 4.2 m — 1.6 m above flood stage
- **Flood extent:** 12.4 km² inundated, including residential districts

Three of three FLOOD_WARNING thresholds breached. Significant urban flooding reported in Burgas city centre.

burgas.name: Black Sea winter storm & coastal inundation
burgas.summary: Force-10 north-easterly drove a 1.8 m storm surge onto the Burgas coast; port infrastructure and low-lying wetlands flooded.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH coastal gauge archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

burgas.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 21 February 2006.** A deep low-pressure system over the Black Sea generated sustained north-easterly winds exceeding 80 km/h, driving a **1.8 m storm surge** onto the Burgas coastline.

- **Surge height:** 1.8 m above mean sea level at Burgas port gauge
- **7-day precipitation:** 88 mm — saturated soils prevented surge drainage
- **Flood extent:** 7.8 km² of the Mandra-Poda wetland complex inundated
- **River level:** Sredetska river at 3.6 m — moderate flood stage

Two of three FLOOD_WATCH thresholds breached. Coastal road closures and port suspension.

burgas.name: Tundzha basin autumn floods
burgas.summary: Prolonged autumn rainfall saturated the Tundzha catchment; river overtopped its banks across the Yambol–Burgas border zone.
burgas.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 16 November 2012.** Six weeks of above-average autumn rainfall brought the **Tundzha river** to flood stage across the western Burgas lowland, inundating agricultural land on the oblast boundary.

- **7-day precipitation:** 105 mm — persistent frontal system over SE Bulgaria
- **Soil moisture:** 87% — soils at field capacity since late October
- **River level:** Tundzha at 4.8 m near Karnobat — 0.9 m above flood threshold
- **Flood extent:** 5.3 km² primarily agricultural

Two of three FLOOD_WATCH thresholds breached. No casualties; road closures in the Aytos area.

burgas.name: Black Sea coast heatwave & drought
burgas.summary: Record coastal temperatures (>41°C) and zero rainfall for six weeks devastated irrigated crops and drained Mandra reservoir.

snapshot.source: ERA5 reanalysis + NIMH temperature archive (TODO: NIMH-verify)

burgas.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 28 July 2007.** The 2007 Black Sea heatwave drove Burgas to **41°C** — unprecedented for a coastal station — while six weeks of near-zero rainfall collapsed soil moisture across the Thracian lowland.

- **Temperature:** 41°C peak — exceeded the DROUGHT_WARNING heat threshold
- **30-day precipitation:** 5 mm — effectively zero; aquifer recharge nil
- **Soil moisture:** 11% — below permanent wilting point for most crops
- **NDVI:** 0.19 — severe vegetation stress visible in Sentinel-2 imagery
- **SPI-3 (drought index):** 3.1 — extreme meteorological drought

Mandra reservoir fell to 28% capacity. Irrigated sunflower and maize yields cut by >50%.

burgas.name: September 2019 Burgas flash floods
burgas.summary: Mediterranean back-trajectory storm brought 85 mm in 3 h to the Burgas plain; road network cut, basement flooding across Pomorie.
burgas.reasoning:
**Historical reconstruction — 7 September 2019.** A slow-moving Mediterranean cyclone funnelled warm moist air onto the Burgas coast, releasing **85 mm in under 3 hours** over the city and Pomorie coastal strip.

- **7-day precipitation:** 132 mm — two successive extreme-rainfall days
- **Soil moisture:** 88% — late-summer soils still partially saturated from August rain
- **River level:** Aheloy stream at 3.9 m — flash peak, rapid recession
- **Flood extent:** 9.7 km² including residential and tourist-zone areas

Three of three FLOOD_WARNING thresholds breached. Significant infrastructure damage; tourist season disrupted.
